# Narration script: Sounding walkthrough (4:01)

Read at a relaxed pace. Each block's time window matches the video exactly, and the word counts are sized for a
calm speaking speed.

**Recording tips**
- Record in one go, or one block at a time. Pause for about 2 seconds between blocks.
- If you stumble, pause, then say the sentence again from the start. I'll keep the clean take.
- Don't rush to fit the times. If a block runs long, I hold the video on that screen a little longer, so nothing gets cut.
- Speak as if you're showing a colleague your screen. Sentences like "I did this because…" are the ones reviewers want.

---

### 1 · 0:00 – 0:10 · Title card
Hi, I'm Hamza. This is Sounding, my version of Fathom: an AI notetaker that turns a meeting recording into a transcript, notes, action items and clips.

### 2 · 0:10 – 0:14 · Login page
The live link works for anyone. Reviewers get in with one click.

### 3 · 0:14 – 0:29 · My calls
This is the meetings list. It's seeded with real recorded meetings, and everything you see here was generated by the pipeline: the titles, the meeting types, the one-line summaries, who spoke and how many action items are still open.

### 4 · 0:29 – 0:43 · The 8-person meeting, speakers
I started with the hardest case: an hour-long meeting with eight people. My first speaker model could only tell four voices apart, so I tested it against human labels and added a second pass that clusters voices. It now separates seven speakers, with far fewer mix-ups.

### 5 · 0:43 – 0:54 · Playback and transcript
When you press play, the transcript follows along with the recording. Clicking any line jumps straight to that moment, so you never have to scrub through an hour.

### 6 · 0:54 – 1:03 · Notes with timestamps
The notes are grouped into sections, and every point links back to where it was said. If the model cites a time that doesn't exist, I throw it away.

### 7 · 1:03 – 1:14 · Templates and action items
Changing the template rewrites the notes for that kind of meeting, like a sales call. Action items keep who said them and when, and you can assign each one to a teammate.

### 8 · 1:14 – 1:27 · Ask this meeting
You can also just ask the meeting a question. Here I'm asking what they decided about collecting more data. The answer comes back with timestamps, and each one takes you to the exact point in the call.

### 9 · 1:27 – 1:46 · Highlight and clip
The highlight button saves the last twenty seconds and the next ten, because by the time you think "that was important", the moment has already passed. You can also clip any range from the transcript. Then you can share just that clip with someone who wasn't on the call.

### 10 · 1:46 – 2:01 · Opening the clip logged out
To show it really works, I log out completely and open the link. The clip plays with its own transcript, and nothing else from the meeting is exposed.

### 11 · 2:01 – 2:21 · Search and Ask across meetings
Back in, search runs across every transcript and every set of notes, and results open right at the matching moment. Ask Sounding does the same thing across all your calls. It pulls the relevant parts from each meeting and answers with links to where each point came from.

### 12 · 2:21 – 2:36 · Trackers
Trackers watch for topics across every call. Keyword trackers look for exact words, and AI trackers look for meaning. So a deadline tracker catches "we need this by Friday" even though nobody said the word deadline.

### 13 · 2:36 – 2:47 · Coaching
Coaching shows talk time, questions and long monologues for each person. Scorecards grade each call against the criteria set for that type of meeting.

### 14 · 2:47 – 3:04 · Playlists, companies and sharing
Playlists collect clips from different meetings, and play all runs them back to back, which is handy for onboarding. Companies are grouped automatically from attendee emails. Every meeting can be private, shared with a team or shared with the whole organisation.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Graphics pass: burn-in subtitles, chapter chips, fast-forward badges and a progress bar.

Usage:
    python3 graphics.py [IN]        # IN defaults to the scratchpad polish directory (see BRIEF.md)

Reads IN/base.edit.json, ../words.json (ASR word timings of the original recording) and docs/NARRATION.md.
Writes IN/out/graphics/:
    overlay.ass     all graphics as one libass script (1920x1080, fixed screen positions)
    subtitles.srt   plain subtitles for upload platforms
    cues.json       the subtitle cues with word-level detail (for checking)
    filter.txt      the ffmpeg -vf chain that burns overlay.ass onto a 1920x1080 video
    fonts/          Schibsted Grotesk static instances (made from the Google Fonts variable font, OFL)

Subtitle text: ASR words are aligned per narration block to the script (Needleman-Wunsch on words with a
fuzzy similarity). Matched and near-matched words take the script's spelling, case and punctuation; words he
said that aren't in the script keep the ASR text; script words he didn't say are dropped. A short curated list
(ASR_FIXES) fixes recognition errors too far from the script for the fuzzy match, and removes self-corrections.
"""

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SCRATCH = "/tmp/claude-0/-root/a2db516c-9100-4760-bff1-2f9fe28ddb93/scratchpad"
IN = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else f"{SCRATCH}/polish")
OUT = f"{IN}/out/graphics"
FONTS = f"{OUT}/fonts"

W, H, TOTAL = E["width"], E["height"], E["total"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fonts
FONT_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/schibstedgrotesk/"
SUB_FONT, UI_FONT = "Schibsted Grotesk SemiBold", "Schibsted Grotesk Medium"


def make_fonts():
    """Downloads the variable font from the Google Fonts repo and cuts static 600/500 instances (libass can't
    pick a weight from a variable font). Returns an advance-width measurer, or None to fall back to DejaVu."""
    os.makedirs(f"{FONTS}/src", exist_ok=True)
    var = f"{FONTS}/src/SchibstedGrotesk[wght].ttf"
    try:
        if not os.path.exists(var):
            import urllib.request

            urllib.request.urlretrieve(FONT_URL + "OFL.txt", f"{FONTS}/OFL.txt")
        from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
        from fontTools.varLib.instancer import instantiateVariableFont
    except Exception as e:
        print("font unavailable, falling back to DejaVu Sans:", e)
        return None
    faces = {}
    for weight, style in [(600, "SemiBold"), (500, "Medium")]:
        path = f"{FONTS}/SchibstedGrotesk-{style}.ttf"
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            f = instantiateVariableFont(TTFont(var), {"wght": weight})
            names = f["name"]
            for nid in (16, 17, 25):
                names.removeNames(nameID=nid)
            for nid, val in [(1, f"Schibsted Grotesk {style}"), (2, "Regular"), (4, f"Schibsted Grotesk {style}"),
                             (6, f"SchibstedGrotesk-{style}")]:

            f["OS/2"].usWeightClass = 400  # its own family, so libass never synthesises bold
            f.save(path)
        f = TTFont(path)
        faces[f"Schibsted Grotesk {style}"] = (f.getBestCmap(), f["hmtx"].metrics,
                                                f["OS/2"].usWinAscent + f["OS/2"].usWinDescent)
    return faces

    SUB_FONT = UI_FONT = "DejaVu Sans"


def em_to_fs(em):
    """ASS \\fs for a given em size in px: libass sizes a font by winAscent+winDescent, not by the em."""
    if FACES is None:
        return round(em * 1.16)
    f = FACES[SUB_FONT]
    return round(em * f[2] / 2048)


def text_width(text, font, fs):
    if FACES is None:
        return len(text) * fs * 0.55
    cmap, hmtx, units = FACES[font]
    w = sum(hmtx[cmap.get(ord(c), cmap[ord("n")])][0] for c in text)
    return w * fs / units

    ("Amza.", "Hamza."), ("Ritham,", "Fathom,"), ("note taker", "notetaker"), ("you did", "seeded"),
    ("summarizers.", "summaries,"), ("an R.", "an hour."), ("note exits,", "doesn't exist,"),

    ("MyAgent", "and my agent"), ("Back-in", "Back in,"), ("Speaker Split", "speaker-split"),
    ("scoreboards, grades, and", "Scorecards grade"), ("scoreboard", "scorecards"),
    ("said that, them", "said them"), ("range of the transcript from", "range from"),
    ("to be titled", "to titled"),
]
DROP_AT = [(77.36, "Now,")]  # a lone "Now," at the very end of block 6, before block 7 starts its own sentence
NAMES = {"hamza": "Hamza", "sounding": "Sounding", "fathom": "Fathom", "qwen": "Qwen", "parakeet": "Parakeet",
         "sortformer": "Sortformer", "titanet": "TitaNet", "google": "Google", "meet": "Meet", "spiced": "SPICED",
         "ai": "AI", "i": "I", "friday": "Friday"}
EXPAND = {"I'm": "I am", "I'd": "I would", "wasn't": "was not"}  # he says these in full; compare like with like
NUM = {"4": "four", "7": "seven", "8": "eight", "10": "ten", "20": "twenty"}
SHOW_NUM = {"twenty": "20"}  # style: numbers above ten as digits


def norm(w):
    w = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9'-]", "", w.lower().replace("’", "'")).strip("-'")
    return NUM.get(w, w)


def sim(a, b):
    a, b = norm(a), norm(b)
    return 1.0 if a == b else difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()


def load_asr():
    words = [w for w in json.load(open(WORDS)) if not any(abs(w[1] - t) < 0.05 and w[0] == s for t, s in DROP_AT)]
    for bad, good in ASR_FIXES:
        bad, good = bad.split(), good.split()
        i = 0
        while i <= len(words) - len(bad):
            if [w[0] for w in words[i:i + len(bad)]] == bad:
                t0, t1 = words[i][1], words[i + len(bad) - 1][2]
                total = sum(len(g) + 1 for g in good)
                new, t = [], t0
                for g in good:  # spread the span over the new words by length
                    d = (t1 - t0) * (len(g) + 1) / total
                    new.append([g, round(t, 3), round(t + d, 3)])
                    t += d
                words[i:i + len(bad)] = new
                i += len(good)
            else:
                i += 1
    return words


def script_blocks():
    txt = open(SCRIPT).read()
    return [m.group(2) for m in re.finditer(r"^### (\d+) · [^\n]*\n(.+?)\n", txt, re.M)]


def align(a, s):
    """Needleman-Wunsch over words. Returns [(i or None, j or None)] pairs."""
    GAP = -0.6
    score = lambda x, y: (2 * sim(x, y) - 0.8) if sim(x, y) >= 0.5 else -1.2
    n, m = len(a), len(s)
    D = [[0.0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(1, n + 1): D[i][0] = i * GAP
    for j in range(1, m + 1): D[0][j] = j * GAP
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            D[i][j] = max(D[i - 1][j - 1] + score(a[i - 1], s[j - 1]), D[i - 1][j] + GAP, D[i][j - 1] + GAP)
    out, i, j = [], n, m
    while i or j:
        if i and j and abs(D[i][j] - (D[i - 1][j - 1] + score(a[i - 1], s[j - 1]))) < 1e-9:
            out.append((i - 1, j - 1)); i -= 1; j -= 1
        elif i and abs(D[i][j] - (D[i - 1][j] + GAP)) < 1e-9:
            out.append((i - 1, None)); i -= 1
        else:
            out.append((None, j - 1)); j -= 1
    return out[::-1]


def ends_sentence(w):
    return w.rstrip('"”').endswith((".", "?", "!"))


def build_words():
    """Final-video word list [{w, t0, t1, block, src}] with corrected text."""
    asr, scripts, words = load_asr(), script_blocks(), []
    for b in E["blocks"]:
        a0, a1 = b["rec_a0"], b["rec_a1"]
        mine = [w for w in asr if a0 <= (w[1] + w[2]) / 2 <= a1]
        s = " ".join(EXPAND.get(t, t) for t in scripts[b["n"] - 1].split()).split()
        pairs = align([w[0] for w in mine], s)
        out = []
        for k, (i, j) in enumerate(pairs):
            if i is None:
                # script word he didn't say: dropped. If it was the "and" joining two clauses, keep his full stop.
                if s[j] == "and" and out and out[-1]["w"].endswith(",") and out[-1]["asr"].endswith("."):
                    out[-1]["w"] = out[-1]["w"][:-1] + "."
                continue
            w = mine[i]
            if j is not None and sim(w[0], s[j]) >= 0.5:
                text, src = s[j], "script"
                if norm(s[j]) in SHOW_NUM:
                    text = re.sub(r"[A-Za-z]+", SHOW_NUM[norm(s[j])], s[j])
            else:
                text, src = w[0], "asr"
                core = norm(text)
                if core in NAMES:
                    text = re.sub(re.escape(core), NAMES[core], text, flags=re.I)
                prev = out[-1] if out else None
                if prev and prev["src"] == "script" and ends_sentence(prev["w"]) and not ends_sentence(prev["asr"]):
                    prev["w"] = prev["w"].rstrip(".")  # the script ended the sentence here; he carried on
                elif prev is None or ends_sentence(prev["w"]):
                    text = text[0].upper() + text[1:]
                elif core not in NAMES:
                    text = text[0].lower() + text[1:] if not text[:2].isupper() else text
            if src == "script" and out and ends_sentence(out[-1]["w"]) and text[0].islower():
                text = text[0].upper() + text[1:]
            t0 = b["voice_at"] + (w[1] - a0)
            t1 = b["voice_at"] + (min(w[2], a1 + 0.3) - a0)
            out.append(dict(w=text, asr=w[0], src=src, t0=round(t0, 3), t1=round(t1, 3), block=b["n"]))
        if out and not ends_sentence(out[-1]["w"]):
            out[-1]["w"] = out[-1]["w"].rstrip(",:;") + "."
        words += out
    return words


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- segmentation
MAX_LINE, MAX_DUR, MIN_DUR = 42, 6.0, 1.0
WEAK_END = {"a", "an", "the", "to", "of", "for", "with", "and", "or", "from", "by", "in", "on", "at", "that", "my",
            "your", "each", "every", "is", "are", "was", "who", "how", "what", "so", "i", "it's", "any", "just"}


def join(ws):
    return " ".join(w["w"] for w in ws)


def split_lines(ws):
    """Best 1- or 2-line layout of a word list, or None if it doesn't fit."""
    text = join(ws)
    if len(text) <= MAX_LINE and len(text) <= 34:
        return [text], 0.0
    best = None
    if len(text) <= MAX_LINE:
        best = ([text], 1.0)  # a long single line is fine, but a balanced pair can be nicer
    for k in range(1, len(ws)):
        l1, l2 = join(ws[:k]), join(ws[k:])
        if len(l1) > MAX_LINE or len(l2) > MAX_LINE:
            continue
        cost = abs(len(l1) - len(l2)) / 10
        last = ws[k - 1]["w"]
        if last.endswith((",", ".", ":", ";", "?")):
            cost -= 1.0
        if norm(last) in WEAK_END:
            cost += 1.5
        if len(l1) > len(l2) + 8:
            cost += 0.3  # prefer a bottom-heavy pyramid
        if best is None or cost < best[1]:
            best = ([l1, l2], cost)
    return best


def break_cost(ws, k):
    """Cost of ending a cue after word k."""
    w, nxt = ws[k], ws[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(ws) else None
    if nxt is None or nxt["t0"] - w["t1"] > 1.2:
        return 0.0
    gap = nxt["t0"] - w["t1"]
    if ends_sentence(w["w"]):
        c = 0.0
    elif w["w"].endswith((",", ":", ";")):
        c = 1.0
    elif gap > 0.3:
        c = 1.5
    else:
        c = 5.0
    if norm(w["w"]) in WEAK_END:
        c += 3.0
    if w["w"].count('"') % 2 or w["w"].startswith('"') and not w["w"].endswith('"'):
        c += 4.0  # inside a quotation
    return c - min(gap, 0.6)


def segment(ws):
    """Dynamic programme over cue boundaries."""
    INF = float("inf")
    best = [0.0] + [INF] * len(ws)
    back = [0] * (len(ws) + 1)
    for j in range(1, len(ws) + 1):
        for i in range(j - 1, -1, -1):
            seg = ws[i:j]
            if seg[-1]["t1"] - seg[0]["t0"] > MAX_DUR + 0.5:
                break
            if any(seg[k + 1]["t0"] - seg[k]["t1"] > 1.2 for k in range(len(seg) - 1)):
                break
            lay = split_lines(seg)
            if lay is None:
                break
            dur = seg[-1]["t1"] - seg[0]["t0"]
            n = len(join(seg))
            c = 2.0 + break_cost(ws, j - 1) + lay[1]
            c += 2.0 if n < 18 else 0.0
            c += 2.0 if dur < MIN_DUR else 0.0
            c += 0.5 * max(0, dur - 5.0)
            if best[i] + c < best[j]:
                best[j], back[j] = best[i] + c, i
    cuts, j = [], len(ws)
    while j:
        cuts.append((back[j], j)); j = back[j]
    return [ws[i:j] for i, j in cuts[::-1]]


def tidy(line, last):
    line = line.replace('"', "“", 1) if line.count('"') == 2 else line
    line = line.replace('"', "”") if "“" in line else line.replace('"', "“" if line.startswith('"') else "”")
    line = line.replace("'", "’")
    if last:
        line = re.sub(r"[.,;:]+(”?)$", r"\1", line)
    return line


def make_cues(words):
    cues = []
    for seg in segment(words):
        lines = split_lines(seg)[0]
        lines = [tidy(l, k == len(lines) - 1) for k, l in enumerate(lines)]
        cues.append(dict(t0=seg[0]["t0"] - 0.08, t1=seg[-1]["t1"] + 0.25, lines=lines, words=seg))
    for a, b in zip(cues, cues[1:]):
        b["t0"] = max(b["t0"], a["words"][-1]["t1"])
        if a["t1"] - a["t0"] < MIN_DUR:
            a["t1"] = a["t0"] + MIN_DUR
        if b["t0"] - a["t1"] < 0.25 or a["t1"] > b["t0"]:
            a["t1"] = b["t0"]  # close tiny gaps and avoid overlaps
    last = cues[-1]
    last["t1"] = min(TOTAL, max(last["t1"], last["t0"] + MIN_DUR))
    for c in cues:
        c["t0"], c["t1"] = round(max(0, c["t0"]), 2), round(c["t1"], 2)
    return cues

def ts(t):
    t = max(0, t)
    cs = int(round(t * 100))
    return f"{cs // 360000}:{cs // 6000 % 60:02d}:{cs // 100 % 60:02d}.{cs % 100:02d}"


def col(hexrgb, alpha=0):
    r, g, b = hexrgb[1:3], hexrgb[3:5], hexrgb[5:7]
    return f"&H{alpha:02X}{b}{g}{r}&".upper().replace("&H", "&H", 1)


def rrect(x0, y0, x1, y1, r):
    """ASS drawing of a rounded rectangle."""
    k = r * 0.4477  # 1 - 0.5523, cubic approximation of a quarter circle
    f = lambda v: f"{v:.1f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
    p = [f"m {f(x0 + r)} {f(y0)}", f"l {f(x1 - r)} {f(y0)}", f"b {f(x1 - k)} {f(y0)} {f(x1)} {f(y0 + k)} {f(x1)} {f(y0 + r)}",
         f"l {f(x1)} {f(y1 - r)}", f"b {f(x1)} {f(y1 - k)} {f(x1 - k)} {f(y1)} {f(x1 - r)} {f(y1)}",
         f"l {f(x0 + r)} {f(y1)}", f"b {f(x0 + k)} {f(y1)} {f(x0)} {f(y1 - k)} {f(x0)} {f(y1 - r)}",
         f"l {f(x0)} {f(y0 + r)}", f"b {f(x0)} {f(y0 + k)} {f(x0 + k)} {f(y0)} {f(x0 + r)} {f(y0)}"]
    return " ".join(p)
